notes: Employees may decline hours not on the originally posted schedule.
Right to rest premium is 1.5x for hours worked within the <10 h gap between a closing and the next opening shift.

Coverage (OLS Q&A § C.1): retail or food-service employers with 500 or more employees worldwide (franchise networks aggregated); full-service restaurants also need 40+ full-service locations worldwide. Applies to hourly employees working in Seattle.

Additional compensation (OLS Q&A § H): added hours (any amount) = 1 h at the scheduled rate, pro-rated for additions under 1 h; date/time change with no loss of hours = 1 h; subtraction of hours (incl. sent home early) or on-call not called in = 1/2 x hours not worked at the scheduled rate. Changes under 15 minutes are a grace period; multiple changes to one shift are netted. Premiums are not part of the regular rate for overtime.

Exceptions (OLS Q&A § I.1): employee-requested change documented in writing; employee shift swaps or coverage; voluntary acceptance of a written 'mass communication' (2+ employees) for hours another employee cannot work; voluntary acceptance of an 'in-person group communication' to 2+ currently working employees for unanticipated customer needs (consecutive hours, i.e. extensions); Access to Hours offers; documented discipline; emergencies.

Call-out repair: a one-on-one call or text to a single employee is NOT exempt (Q&A § I.10 Example 1: 1 hour owed). The mass-communication exception does not cover open shifts or hours other than the absent employee's actual hours, and never applies to sending someone home early. Employees may decline any hours not on the originally posted schedule.

No tip credit: since January 1, 2025 small employers may no longer count tips toward minimum compensation (Seattle OLS minimum wage page); state law also forbids it (RCW 49.46.020(3)). No tipped_minimum_wage rule.

rules.summary: Inside 14 days, Seattle pays 1 hour at the scheduled rate for added hours (pro-rated under 1 h; changes under 15 min exempt) or a moved shift, and half the hours not worked for cuts. Hours accepted from a written 'mass communication' covering an absent coworker are exempt.
